outputs.explanation: Panel A is a photograph of intestines, not a quantitative plot, so the check does not apply.
Panel B consists of histology micrographs, not a plot of averaged data, so the check does not apply.

The top box plot summarizes total polyp number per mouse across genotypes (n=8–18 per genotype per caption) using only median/quartile/whisker statistics, with no individual mouse data points overlaid. The lower 3D bar chart similarly shows mean polyp number per diameter category per genotype without any individual data points or error bars. Both graphs aggregate data across multiple animals but fail to show the underlying individual measurements.

Panel D is a Kaplan–Meier survival curve, a cumulative/step-function representation of time-to-event data rather than an average with variance; individual data points are not conventionally overlaid on survival curves, so this format is acceptable.

The bar graph quantifying GTP-bound Rac1 and Cdc42 (normalized to total protein) presents only mean bars (with a small error indicator) derived from what appears to be replicate experiments/blots, but no individual data points from the individual replicates are shown.
Panel F shows immunohistochemistry micrographs, not a quantitative averaged plot, so the check does not apply.

The bottom bar graph quantifying relative expression of Asef, pJNK1 and MMP9 (with error bars and significance asterisks) shows only mean ± error values across conditions, with no individual data points from the replicate samples/experiments plotted.
